observations: SNL36:015-018 gives four M4131 bracket assemblies, each with a quarter-inch by two-inch split pin. SNL170:007 assigns two half-inch by2-1/8inch rivets per bracket, total8.

SNL72:026 and73:001-004 rear-control composition lists four M4137 spring washers, two M4132 foot-brake horizontal levers and one each M4133/M4134 low-brake lever plus the channel assembly. This supports assigning one washer and one retained lever to each fulcrum; the exact washer form is not printed.

HB104 shows vertical pedestal pivots with circular shoulders and horizontal levers. The mounting-foot outline and fastener axes are obscured; the cast-foot/vertical-rivet hypothesis below is an approximation, not an observation.

SNL6 plan locates the outer foot-brake pivots nearer the forward channel edge and inner low-brake pivots rearward. Rod-end stations guide lever ratios and clocking; this segmented schematic is not globally calibrated.
M4129 has a floor bolt but no separate rivet application. This increment does not assign invented rivets or establish its mounting topology.
hypotheses: M4131 has a thick cast foot with two vertical rivets through the upper channel web, a round thrust shoulder and integral vertical journal.25.4mm estimated foot stock plus6.35mm channel gives31.75mm grip, allowing the literal53.975mm rivet shank stock to form a conventional1.75D tail without trimming.

Four fulcrums atY+/-710 and+/-450mm follow the existing conditional transverse layout. Outer pivots lie over the forward flange; inner pivots cantilever25.4mm rearward of the rear flange to reproduce the separate neighboring eye stations without merging geometry.
Bracket foot overhang is intentional; both rivet pads must fully bear on channel material. This is not a full-foot seating or load-capacity claim.

Each M4132 uses the same straight double-arm lever definition at different clockings. Distinct low-lever profiles use the separately estimated front/brake vectors from their plan picks. All hub, stock and bore dimensions are estimates.

M4137 is initially represented as a compressed flat annular spring washer above the lever. Its free form is unknown. The split pin spreads horizontally to clear the washer and supplies axial retention.
limits: HB five fulcrums and center M4131/M1431 identity remain open; this rear assembly follows the internally consistent SNL four.
No source declares the pivot diameter, casting footprint, rivet orientation, lever stock/bores or washer dimensions. Native fit cannot establish these historical facts.
The source plan is used to form geometry, not as an independent camera validation. The existing SNL6 side registration remains fixed for diagnostic projection.
M4129, spring brackets, rods and complete service paths remain subsequent work.
